questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given below are certain reactions. Identify the reaction for which $K_p \neq K_c$ :
questions.solution:
The relation between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$, where $\Delta n_g$ is the difference between the number of moles of gaseous products and gaseous reactants.

For $K_p \neq K_c$, $\Delta n_g$ must be non-zero.

For $\text{H}_2\text{O (g)} + \text{CO (g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow K_p = K_c$

For $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2 \Rightarrow K_p \neq K_c$

For $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI (g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow K_p = K_c$

For $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO (g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow K_p = K_c$

Answer: $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$

$\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{~g})+3 \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{~g}), \Delta \mathrm{H}=-\mathrm{Q}$
Reaction is favoured in forward direction by:
options: low pressure, high temperature and high concentration of ammonia
high pressure, low temperature and higher concentration of $\mathrm{H}_2$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{~g})+3 \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{~g}), \Delta \mathrm{H}=-\mathrm{Q}$
According to Le Chatelier's principle.
- Exothermic reactions are favoured at low temperature.
- Increase in pressure shifts the reaction in direction having lesser number of moles. Hence, the given reaction shifts forward on increasing pressure.
- Increasing the concentration of reactants shifts the reaction in forward direction. So high concentration of $\mathrm{H}_2$ shifts reaction in forward direction.

questions.q:
The dissociation constants for acetic acid and $\mathrm{HCN}$ at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ are $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$ and $4.5 \times 10^{-10}$, respectively. The equilibrium constant for the equilibrium,
$\mathrm{CN}^{-}+\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH} \quad \mathrm{HCN}+\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}$
would be
questions.solution:
Given, $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}+\mathrm{H}^{+}$
\begin{array}{r}
\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=1.5 \times 10^{-5} \ldots \text { (i) } \\
\mathrm{HCN} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{CN}^{-} ; \quad \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=4.5 \times 10^{-10} \ldots \text { (ii) } \\
\mathrm{CN}^{-}+\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HCN}+\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-} \\
\mathrm{K}=\text { ? }
\end{array}

On substracting Eq. (ii) from Eq. (i), we get

\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{CN}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HCN}+\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-} ; \\
& \mathrm{K}=\frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_1}}=\frac{1.5 \times 10^{-5}}{4.5 \times 10^{-10}}=\frac{10^5}{3}=3.33 \times 10^4
\end{aligned}

While adding two equations, dissociation constants are multiplied and when subtracting the equations, dissociation constants are divided.
Alternative

\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}+\mathrm{H}^{+} ; \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=1.5 \times 10^{-5} \\
& \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}\right]\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}\right]}=1.5 \times 10^{-5} \\
& \mathrm{HCN} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{CN}^{-} ; \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=4.5 \times 10^{-10} \\
& \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]\left[\mathrm{CN}^{-}\right]}{[\mathrm{HCN}]}=4.5 \times 10^{-10} \\
& \mathrm{CN}^{-}+\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HCN}+\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-} \\
& \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{[\mathrm{HCN}]\left[\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{CN}^{-}\right]\left[\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}\right]} \\
&
\end{aligned}

From Eqs. (i), (ii) and (iii),

\mathrm{K}_c=\frac{1.5 \times 10^{-5}}{4.5 \times 10^{-10}}=3.33 \times 10^4

The following equilibrium constant are given:
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{N}_2+3 \mathrm{H}_2 & \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NH}_3 ; \mathrm{K}_1 \\
\mathrm{~N}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 & \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO} ; \mathrm{K}_2 \\
\mathrm{H}_2+1 / 2 \mathrm{O}_2 & \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} ; \mathrm{K}_3
\end{aligned}$
The equilibrium constant for the oxidation of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ by oxygen to give $\mathrm{NO}$ is:
questions.solution:
Given,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{N}_2+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NH}_3 ; \mathrm{K}_1 \\
& \mathrm{~N}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO} ; \mathrm{K}_2 \\
& \mathrm{H}_2+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} ; \mathrm{K}_3
\end{aligned}$
We have to calculate
$\begin{aligned}
& 4 \mathrm{NH}_3+5 \mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} ; \mathrm{K}=\text { ? } \\
& \text { or } 2 \mathrm{NH}_3+\frac{5}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NO}+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}
\end{aligned}$
For this equation $\mathrm{K}=\frac{[\mathrm{NO}]^2\left[\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right]^3}{\left[\mathrm{NH}_3\right]^2\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]^{5 / 2}}$ but
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{K}_1 & =\frac{\left[\mathrm{NH}_3\right]^2}{\left[\mathrm{~N}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]^3} \\
\mathrm{~K}_2 & =\frac{[\mathrm{NO}]^2}{\left[\mathrm{~N}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]} \\
\mathrm{K}_3 & =\frac{\left[\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]^{1 / 2}} \\
\mathrm{~K}_3 & =\frac{\left[\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}^3\right.}{\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]^3\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]^{3 / 2}}
\end{aligned}$
Now
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{K}_2 \cdot \mathrm{K}_3{ }^3}{\mathrm{~K}_1} =\frac{[\mathrm{NO}]^2}{\left[\mathrm{~N}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]} \times \frac{\left[\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right]^3}{\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]^3\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]^{3 / 2}} \times \frac{\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]^3}{\left[\mathrm{NH}_3\right]^2} \\
& =\frac{[\mathrm{NO}]^2\left[\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right]^3}{\left[\mathrm{NH}_3\right]^2\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]^{5 / 2}}=\mathrm{K} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{K}=\frac{\mathrm{K}_2 \cdot \mathrm{K}_3{ }^3}{\mathrm{~K}_1}
\end{aligned}$

- Reason (R): Equilibrium constant is independent of temperature.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements; one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A) : In the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) at constant pressure and temperature addition of helium at equilibrium increases the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\).
Reason (R) : Equilibrium constant changes only with change in temperature.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): In the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) at constant pressure and temperature, addition of helium at equilibrium increases the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\).
Correct.
Reaction:
\(\mathrm{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(g)+\mathrm{Cl}_2(g)\)
Number of moles increases (\(1 \rightarrow 2\)).
- If He is added at constant volume, no effect on equilibrium (only partial pressures change proportionally).
- If He is added at constant pressure, the system volume increases. Partial pressures of reactants and products decrease, shifting equilibrium towards more gaseous moles \(\rightarrow\) increased dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\).
- Reason (R): Equilibrium constant changes only with change in temperature.
Correct. This is a fundamental property of equilibrium constants.
But \(X(\mathrm{R})\) is not the correct explanation of \((\mathrm{A})\).
The shift of equilibrium with helium addition is explained by Le Chatelier's Principle and change in partial pressures, not by equilibrium constant.

questions.subject: Chemistry

Assertion (A) : Solubility of a gas in water decreases with increase in temperature.
Reason (R) : Dissolution of a gas in water is an exothermic process.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): Solubility of a gas in water decreases with increase in temperature.
Correct.
Most gases dissolve in water exothermically. According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium in the opposite direction (less dissolution), hence solubility decreases.
- Reason (R): Dissolution of a gas in water is an exothermic process.
Correct.
Heat is released when gas molecules are captured by water molecules (due to intermolecular attractions).
Here, (R) correctly explains (A) \(\rightarrow\) higher temperature adds heat, so equilibrium shifts to gas phase, reducing solubility.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the exothermic oxidation of sulfur dioxide at equilibrium:

$2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \text{Heat}$

Which of the following actions will decrease the equilibrium yield of $\mathrm{SO}_3$?
options: Adding an inert gas at constant volume
Adding an inert gas at constant pressure
questions.solution:
The given reaction is exothermic. According to Le Chatelier's principle, decreasing the temperature will shift the equilibrium in the forward direction, increasing the yield of $\mathrm{SO}_3$.

The number of gaseous moles on the reactant side is $2 + 1 = 3$, and on the product side is $2$. Since $\Delta n_g = 2 - 3 = -1$, increasing the pressure will shift the equilibrium towards the side with fewer gaseous moles (forward direction), increasing the yield of $\mathrm{SO}_3$.

Adding an inert gas at constant volume does not change the partial pressures or molar concentrations of the reacting gases, so the equilibrium state is unaffected.

Adding an inert gas at constant pressure increases the total volume of the system. This decreases the partial pressures of all reacting gases, causing the equilibrium to shift towards the direction with more gaseous moles (backward direction) to oppose the change. This backward shift will decrease the equilibrium yield of $\mathrm{SO}_3$.

Answer: Adding an inert gas at constant pressure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the synthesis of ammonia ($\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$), the numerical value of $K_p$ is smaller than $K_c$ at $298\text{ K}$.

Reason (R): $K_p$ and $K_c$ are related by the expression $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$, where $\Delta n$ is the difference between the total number of moles of all products and all reactants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: For the reaction $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$, the change in gaseous moles is $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$.
The relation is $K_p = K_c(RT)^{-2} = \dfrac{K_c}{(RT)^2}$.
At $298\text{ K}$, the value of $RT$ is approximately $0.0831 \times 298 \approx 24.76 \text{ L bar K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$, which is significantly greater than $1$. Thus, $(RT)^2 \gt 1$, making $K_p \lt K_c$.

Reason (R) is incorrect: The term $\Delta n$ (or $\Delta n_g$) in the relation $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$ specifically represents the difference between the number of moles of gaseous products and gaseous reactants, not all products and all reactants. Solids and liquids must be excluded from this calculation.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For an equilibrium reaction, if all stoichiometric coefficients of the balanced chemical equation are multiplied by 2, the new equilibrium constant becomes the square of the original equilibrium constant.

Reason (R): The numerical value of the equilibrium constant for a reaction depends on the stoichiometric representation of the balanced chemical equation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
The equilibrium constant expression is written by raising the active masses of reactants and products to the power of their respective stoichiometric coefficients. Thus, the numerical value of the equilibrium constant depends on the stoichiometric representation of the balanced chemical equation. Therefore, (R) is true.

When all stoichiometric coefficients of a balanced chemical equation are multiplied by a factor of 2, the new equilibrium constant is the original equilibrium constant raised to the power of 2 (i.e., it is squared). Therefore, (A) is true.

Since the dependence of the equilibrium constant on stoichiometric coefficients is the underlying reason for the squaring effect, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the Haber process for the synthesis of ammonia, $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$, the equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is $4.0 \times 10^{-4}$ at $500\text{ K}$. If the backward reaction rate constant $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}$ at this temperature is $2.0 \times 10^{-2}$, what is the value of the forward reaction rate constant $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}$?

[Given: $\mathrm{R} = 0.08\text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
For the reaction $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$, the change in the number of moles of gaseous species is:
$\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$

The relationship between $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}}$

Rearranging to solve for $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}}{(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}}} = \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}(\mathrm{RT})^2$

Calculate $\mathrm{RT}$:
$\mathrm{RT} = 0.08 \times 500 = 40$

Now, substitute the values to find $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = (4.0 \times 10^{-4}) \times (40)^2 = (4.0 \times 10^{-4}) \times 1600 = 0.64$

The equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is also given by the ratio of the forward and backward rate constants:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}$

Solving for $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}$:
$\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}} = \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} \times \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}} = 0.64 \times (2.0 \times 10^{-2}) = 1.28 \times 10^{-2}$

Answer: $1.28 \times 10^{-2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the equilibrium reaction $2\text{NO}_{2}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_{2}\text{O}_{4}(\text{g})$, the equilibrium constant $K_{c}$ is $4.0 \times 10^{3}$ at a certain temperature. If the equilibrium concentration of $\text{N}_{2}\text{O}_{4}$ is $0.1\text{ M}$, what is the equilibrium concentration of $\text{NO}_{2}$?
questions.solution:
The equilibrium constant expression for the given reaction is:
$K_{c} = \dfrac{[\text{N}_{2}\text{O}_{4}]}{[\text{NO}_{2}]^{2}}$

Substitute the given values into the expression:
$4.0 \times 10^{3} = \dfrac{0.1}{[\text{NO}_{2}]^{2}}$

Rearrange to solve for $[\text{NO}_{2}]^{2}$:
$[\text{NO}_{2}]^{2} = \dfrac{0.1}{4.0 \times 10^{3}} = \dfrac{1}{40000} = 25 \times 10^{-6}$

Taking the square root of both sides gives the concentration of $\text{NO}_{2}$:
$[\text{NO}_{2}] = 5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$

Common mistakes:
- Forgetting to take the square root leads to $2.5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ M}$.
- Inverting the $K_{c}$ expression leads to $20\text{ M}$ or $400\text{ M}$.

Answer: $5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Solid ammonium hydrosulfide is placed in a closed vessel and allowed to decompose at $600 \mathrm{~K}$ until equilibrium is reached:
$\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{HS}(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{g})$
If the total pressure of the gas mixture at equilibrium is $20 \mathrm{~bar}$, what is the value of $K_c$ for this reaction at $600 \mathrm{~K}$?
(Given: $\mathrm{R} = 0.0833 \mathrm{~L~bar~K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The thermal decomposition of solid ammonium hydrosulfide is given by:
$\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{HS}(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{g})$

At equilibrium, the gases are produced in a $1:1$ molar ratio. Let the partial pressure of each gas be $p$.
Total pressure, $P_{\text{total}} = P_{\mathrm{NH}_3} + P_{\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}} = p + p = 2p$
Given $P_{\text{total}} = 20 \mathrm{~bar}$, we have $2p = 20 \implies p = 10 \mathrm{~bar}$.

The equilibrium constant in terms of partial pressures ($K_p$) is:
$K_p = P_{\mathrm{NH}_3} \times P_{\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}} = 10 \times 10 = 100$

The change in the number of moles of gas is:
$\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 0 = 2$

The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is:
$K_p = K_c(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta n_g}$

Given $\mathrm{R} = 0.0833 \mathrm{~L~bar~K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ (which is approximately $\dfrac{1}{12}$) and $\mathrm{T} = 600 \mathrm{~K}$:
$\mathrm{RT} = 0.0833 \times 600 \approx 50 \mathrm{~L~bar~mol}^{-1}$

Substituting the values into the formula:
$100 = K_c(50)^2$
$K_c = \dfrac{100}{2500} = 0.04$

Using the total pressure directly as $K_p$ leads to the incorrect value $0.008$, and forgetting to square $\mathrm{RT}$ leads to $2.0$.

Answer: $0.04$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate occurs in a closed vessel according to the following equation:

$\text{CaCO}_3(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO}(\text{s}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g})$

If $2.0\text{ moles}$ of $\text{CaCO}_3$ are placed in a $10.0\text{ L}$ closed vessel and allowed to reach equilibrium at a certain temperature, the equilibrium constant $K_c$ for the reaction is found to be $0.05\text{ M}$. What is the equilibrium concentration of $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$?
questions.solution:
The given reaction is a heterogeneous equilibrium:
$\text{CaCO}_3(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO}(\text{s}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g})$

By convention, the active masses (molar concentrations) of pure solids and pure liquids are taken as unity and are excluded from the equilibrium constant expression.

Therefore, the equilibrium constant $K_c$ depends only on the concentration of the gaseous product:
$K_c = [\text{CO}_2(\text{g})]$

Given that $K_c = 0.05\text{ M}$, the equilibrium concentration of $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ is simply equal to the value of $K_c$.

$[\text{CO}_2(\text{g})] = 0.05\text{ M}$

The initial moles of $\text{CaCO}_3$ and the volume of the vessel do not change the equilibrium concentration of the gas as long as some solid remains.

Answer: $0.05\text{ M}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the equilibrium reaction of the formation of nitric oxide:
$\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}), \Delta \mathrm{H} = +180.7 \text{ kJ}$
Which of the following conditions will favour the maximum yield of $\mathrm{NO}$?
options: High temperature, high pressure and high concentration of $\mathrm{N}_2$
High temperature, high concentration of $\mathrm{O}_2$, and pressure has no effect
Low temperature, high pressure and high concentration of $\mathrm{N}_2$
Low temperature, low pressure and low concentration of $\mathrm{O}_2$
questions.solution:
According to Le Chatelier's principle:

1. The given reaction is endothermic ($\Delta \mathrm{H} \gt 0$). Endothermic reactions are favoured in the forward direction at high temperatures.

2. The change in the number of gaseous moles is $\Delta \mathrm{n}_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$. Since there is no change in the number of moles of gases, a change in pressure has no effect on the equilibrium position.

3. Increasing the concentration of reactants ($\mathrm{N}_2$ or $\mathrm{O}_2$) shifts the equilibrium in the forward direction to consume the added reactants.

Therefore, high temperature and high concentration of $\mathrm{O}_2$ favour the maximum yield of $\mathrm{NO}$, while pressure has no effect.

Answer: High temperature, high concentration of $\mathrm{O}_2$, and pressure has no effect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the reaction $2\mathrm{SO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$, the ratio $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c}$ decreases as temperature increases.

Reason (R): For this reaction, the number of moles of gaseous products is greater than the number of moles of gaseous reactants ($\Delta n_g \gt 0$).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
For the given reaction $2\mathrm{SO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$:
$\Delta n_g = (\text{moles of gaseous products}) - (\text{moles of gaseous reactants})$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (2 + 1) = -1$

Since $\Delta n_g \lt 0$, the Reason (R) is false.

The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is:
$K_p = K_c(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta n_g}$
$\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (\mathrm{RT})^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{RT}}$

As temperature ($\mathrm{T}$) increases, the value of $\mathrm{RT}$ increases, which causes the ratio $\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{RT}}$ to decrease. Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c}$ decreases with an increase in temperature. Thus, the Assertion (A) is true.

Hence, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reaction)List-II ($\dfrac{K_p}{K_c}$ ratio)
(A) $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI(g)}$(I) $(RT)^{-2}$
(B) $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$(II) $1$
(C) $\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO(s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$(III) $(RT)^{-1}$
(D) $2\text{NO}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_4\text{(g)}$(IV) $RT$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$, which rearranges to $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (RT)^{\Delta n_g}$.

For (A) $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI(g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 2 = 0$. Thus, $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (RT)^0 = 1$.

For (B) $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2$. Thus, $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (RT)^{-2}$.

For (C) $\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO(s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$, only gaseous species are considered. $\Delta n_g = 1 - 0 = 1$. Thus, $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (RT)^1 = RT$.

For (D) $2\text{NO}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_4\text{(g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 1 - 2 = -1$. Thus, $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (RT)^{-1}$.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A mixture of $2.0\text{ moles}$ of $\text{SO}_{2}$ and $2.0\text{ moles}$ of $\text{O}_{2}$ is placed in a closed vessel of volume $2.0\text{ L}$ and allowed to reach equilibrium according to the reaction:

$2\text{SO}_{2}(\text{g}) + \text{O}_{2}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_{3}(\text{g})$

At equilibrium, $1.0\text{ mole}$ of $\text{SO}_{3}$ is formed. The value of the equilibrium constant $K_{c}$ for this reaction is:
questions.solution:
Set up an ICE (Initial, Change, Equilibrium) table for the moles of each species:
Initial moles: $\text{SO}_{2} = 2.0$, $\text{O}_{2} = 2.0$, $\text{SO}_{3} = 0$

Since $1.0\text{ mole}$ of $\text{SO}_{3}$ is formed at equilibrium, the change for $\text{SO}_{3}$ is $+1.0\text{ mol}$.
From the stoichiometry of the reaction ($2:1:2$), the change in $\text{SO}_{2}$ is $-1.0\text{ mol}$ and the change in $\text{O}_{2}$ is $-0.5\text{ mol}$.

Equilibrium moles:
$\text{SO}_{2} = 2.0 - 1.0 = 1.0\text{ mol}$
$\text{O}_{2} = 2.0 - 0.5 = 1.5\text{ mol}$
$\text{SO}_{3} = 1.0\text{ mol}$

Convert moles to equilibrium concentrations by dividing by the volume of the vessel ($2.0\text{ L}$):
$[\text{SO}_{2}] = \dfrac{1.0}{2.0} = 0.5\text{ M}$
$[\text{O}_{2}] = \dfrac{1.5}{2.0} = 0.75\text{ M}$
$[\text{SO}_{3}] = \dfrac{1.0}{2.0} = 0.5\text{ M}$

Write the equilibrium constant expression:
$K_{c} = \dfrac{[\text{SO}_{3}]^{2}}{[\text{SO}_{2}]^{2}[\text{O}_{2}]}$

Substitute the equilibrium concentrations:
$K_{c} = \dfrac{(0.5)^{2}}{(0.5)^{2} \times 0.75} = \dfrac{1}{0.75} = \dfrac{4}{3} \approx 1.33$

Common mistakes:
- Using moles directly instead of concentrations gives $0.67$.
- Subtracting $1.0\text{ mol}$ from $\text{O}_{2}$ instead of $0.5\text{ mol}$ gives $2.0$.
- Inverting the $K_{c}$ expression gives $0.75$.

Answer: $1.33$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain gaseous reversible reaction, the unit of the equilibrium constant $K_c$ is $\mathrm{L}^{2} \mathrm{mol}^{-2}$. Which of the following is the correct mathematical relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ for this reaction?
questions.solution:
The unit of the equilibrium constant $K_c$ is given by $(\mathrm{mol\ L}^{-1})^{\Delta n_g}$.

Given unit $= \mathrm{L}^{2} \mathrm{mol}^{-2} = (\mathrm{mol\ L}^{-1})^{-2}$.

Comparing the powers, we get $\Delta n_g = -2$.

The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is:
$K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$

Substituting $\Delta n_g = -2$:
$K_p = K_c(RT)^{-2}$

Rearranging the equation by multiplying both sides by $(RT)^2$ gives:
$K_c = K_p(RT)^{2}$

Answer: $K_c = K_p(RT)^{2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For a hypothetical gas phase reaction $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{D}(\mathrm{g})$, the forward rate constant ($\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}$) is $2.0 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ and the backward rate constant ($\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}$) is $1.0 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. At a given instant, the concentrations of the reacting species are $[\mathrm{A}] = 0.1 \mathrm{~M}$, $[\mathrm{B}] = 0.2 \mathrm{~M}$, $[\mathrm{C}] = 0.2 \mathrm{~M}$, and $[\mathrm{D}] = 0.4 \mathrm{~M}$.

What is the value of the equilibrium constant ($\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$) and the predicted direction in which the reaction will proceed?
questions.solution:
The equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is the ratio of the forward and backward rate constants:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}} = \dfrac{2.0 \times 10^{-3}}{1.0 \times 10^{-3}} = 2.0$

The reaction quotient $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{c}}$ at the given instant is calculated as:
$\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{c}} = \dfrac{[\mathrm{C}][\mathrm{D}]}{[\mathrm{A}][\mathrm{B}]} = \dfrac{0.2 \times 0.4}{0.1 \times 0.2} = \dfrac{0.08}{0.02} = 4.0$

Comparing $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{c}}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$, we find that $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{c}} \gt \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ ($4.0 \gt 2.0$).

Since the reaction quotient is greater than the equilibrium constant, the reaction will proceed in the backward direction to reach equilibrium.

Answer: $2.0$, Backward direction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the thermal decomposition of solid ammonium carbamate,
$\text{NH}_2\text{COONH}_4\text{(s)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$
the ratio of the equilibrium constants $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c}$ is:
questions.solution:
For the given heterogeneous reaction:
$\text{NH}_2\text{COONH}_4\text{(s)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$

The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$.

Here, $\Delta n_g$ is the difference between the number of moles of gaseous products and gaseous reactants.

Moles of gaseous products = $2 \text{ (from NH}_3) + 1 \text{ (from CO}_2) = 3$
Moles of gaseous reactants = $0$ (since ammonium carbamate is a solid and its active mass is taken as unity).

Therefore, $\Delta n_g = 3 - 0 = 3$.

Substituting this value, we get $K_p = K_c(RT)^3$, which gives the ratio $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (RT)^3$.

Answer: $(RT)^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
At a given temperature, the equilibrium constant for the reaction
$\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g})$ is $K_1$.

The equilibrium constant $K_2$ for the reaction
$2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})$
is related to $K_1$ as:
questions.solution:
The given initial reaction is:
$\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) ; K_1$

Reversing this reaction inverses the equilibrium constant:
$\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) ; K' = \dfrac{1}{K_1}$

Multiplying the reversed reaction by a factor of 2 raises the equilibrium constant to the power of 2:
$2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) ; K_2 = (K')^2$

Substituting the value of $K'$:
$K_2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{K_1}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{K_1^2}$

Answer: $K_2 = \dfrac{1}{K_1^2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The equilibrium concentrations for the reaction $\text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \text{I}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}(\text{g})$ at a constant temperature are recorded for two different experiments in the table below:

Experiment$[\text{H}_2]$ in $\text{M}$$[\text{I}_2]$ in $\text{M}$$[\text{HI}]$ in $\text{M}$
1$0.1$$0.1$$0.4$
2$0.1$$x$$0.8$


The value of the missing equilibrium concentration '$x$' is:
questions.solution:
For the reaction $\text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \text{I}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}(\text{g})$, the equilibrium constant $K_c$ is given by:

$K_c = \dfrac{[\text{HI}]^2}{[\text{H}_2][\text{I}_2]}$

Using the data from Experiment 1:
$K_c = \dfrac{(0.4)^2}{(0.1)(0.1)} = \dfrac{0.16}{0.01} = 16$

Since the temperature is constant, $K_c$ remains the same for Experiment 2. Substituting the values from Experiment 2 into the $K_c$ expression:
$16 = \dfrac{(0.8)^2}{(0.1)(x)}$

$16 = \dfrac{0.64}{0.1x}$

$1.6x = 0.64$

$x = 0.4\text{ M}$

The missing concentration is $0.4\text{ M}$.

Answer: $0.4\text{ M}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the equilibrium $\mathrm{CaCO}_3(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CaO(\mathrm{s})} + \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g})$, increasing the pressure at equilibrium decreases the amount of $\mathrm{CaO}(\mathrm{s})$ present.

Reason (R): According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium towards the direction having fewer moles of gaseous substances.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. In the given heterogeneous equilibrium, $\mathrm{CaCO}_3(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CaO}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g})$, the number of gaseous moles on the reactant side is $0$ and on the product side is $1$. When pressure is increased, the equilibrium shifts in the direction that reduces the pressure, which is the direction with fewer moles of gaseous substances (backward direction). This backward shift consumes $\mathrm{CaO}(\mathrm{s})$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g})$ to form more $\mathrm{CaCO}_3(\mathrm{s})$, thereby decreasing the amount of $\mathrm{CaO}(\mathrm{s})$ present.

Reason (R) is true and is the correct explanation for Assertion (A), as it correctly states the principle governing the effect of pressure on equilibrium, which dictates the backward shift in this specific reaction.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain reversible chemical reaction, the equilibrium constants $K_c$ and $K_p$ are related as $\dfrac{K_c}{K_p} = (\mathrm{RT})^2$. Which of the following reactions satisfies this condition?
questions.solution:
The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by:
$K_p = K_c(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta n_g}$

Rearranging the given condition $\dfrac{K_c}{K_p} = (\mathrm{RT})^2$, we get:
$\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (\mathrm{RT})^{-2}$

Comparing this with the standard equation, we find $\Delta n_g = -2$.

Let us calculate $\Delta n_g$ (moles of gaseous products $-$ moles of gaseous reactants) for the given options:
1) $2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$ : $\Delta n_g = (1 + 3) - 2 = +2$
2) $\mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$ : $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$
3) $\mathrm{PCl}_{5(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_{3(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{Cl}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$ : $\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 1 = +1$
4) $\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{I}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{HI}_{(\mathrm{g})}$ : $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$

Thus, the reaction $\mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$ satisfies the given condition.

Answer: $\mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the optimum conditions for maximizing the forward reaction according to Le Chatelier's principle.

List-I (Reactions)List-II (Favourable Conditions)
(A) $2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}); \Delta \mathrm{H} \lt 0$(I) High temperature, High pressure
(B) $2\mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 3\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}); \Delta \mathrm{H} \lt 0$(II) High temperature, Low pressure
(C) $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}); \Delta \mathrm{H} \gt 0$(III) Low temperature, High pressure
(D) $\mathrm{PCl}_5(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g}); \Delta \mathrm{H} \gt 0$(IV) Low temperature, Low pressure

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in temperature favours endothermic reactions ($\Delta \mathrm{H} \gt 0$), while a decrease in temperature favours exothermic reactions ($\Delta \mathrm{H} \lt 0$). An increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer gaseous moles, and a decrease in pressure shifts it towards the side with more gaseous moles.

(A) $2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}); \Delta \mathrm{H} \lt 0$
Exothermic and $\Delta \mathrm{n}_g = 2 - 3 = -1$. Favourably shifted forward by Low temperature and High pressure. Matches with (III).

(B) $2\mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 3\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}); \Delta \mathrm{H} \lt 0$
Exothermic and $\Delta \mathrm{n}_g = 3 - 2 = +1$. Favourably shifted forward by Low temperature and Low pressure. Matches with (IV).

(C) $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}); \Delta \mathrm{H} \gt 0$
Endothermic and $\Delta \mathrm{n}_g = 2 - 3 = -1$. Favourably shifted forward by High temperature and High pressure. Matches with (I).

(D) $\mathrm{PCl}_5(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g}); \Delta \mathrm{H} \gt 0$
Endothermic and $\Delta \mathrm{n}_g = 2 - 1 = +1$. Favourably shifted forward by High temperature and Low pressure. Matches with (II).

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the synthesis of sulphur trioxide gas represented by the equation $2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g})$, the forward reaction rate constant is $1.5 \times 10^3$ and the backward reaction rate constant is $3.0 \times 10^2$ at $300\text{ K}$.

[Given: $\mathrm{R} = \dfrac{1}{12}\text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]

The value of $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ for this reaction at $300\text{ K}$ is:
questions.solution:
The equilibrium constant in terms of concentration, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$, is the ratio of the forward rate constant to the backward rate constant:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}} = \dfrac{1.5 \times 10^3}{3.0 \times 10^2} = 5$

For the reaction $2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g})$, the change in the number of moles of gaseous species is:
$\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$
$\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = 2 - (2 + 1) = -1$

The relationship between $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}}$

Substituting the given values:
$\mathrm{RT} = \dfrac{1}{12} \times 300 = 25$
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = 5 \times (25)^{-1} = \dfrac{5}{25} = 0.2$

Answer: 0.2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the gaseous reaction $\text{PCl}_5\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$, at what temperature will the numerical value of $K_p$ be equal to the numerical value of $K_c$? (Given $R$ is the universal gas constant)
questions.solution:
For the given reaction, $\text{PCl}_5\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$

The change in the number of moles of gaseous species is:
$\Delta n_g = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = 1$

The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by:
$K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$
$K_p = K_c(RT)^1$

For the numerical values of $K_p$ and $K_c$ to be equal, we must have:
$RT = 1$
$T = \dfrac{1}{R}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{R}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

(A)$\mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$(I)$K_p = K_c$
(B)$\mathrm{CaCO}_{3(\mathrm{s})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CaO}_{(\mathrm{s})} + \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$(II)$K_p = K_c(RT)$
(C)$\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{Cl}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{HCl}_{(\mathrm{g})}$(III)$K_p = K_c(RT)^{-2}$
(D)$\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{HS}_{(\mathrm{s})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}_{(\mathrm{g})}$(IV)$K_p = K_c(RT)^{2}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$, where $\Delta n_g = (\text{moles of gaseous products}) - (\text{moles of gaseous reactants})$.

For (A): $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$. Thus, $K_p = K_c(RT)^{-2}$.

For (B): Solids are not included in the calculation of $\Delta n_g$. $\Delta n_g = 1 - 0 = 1$. Thus, $K_p = K_c(RT)$.

For (C): $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$. Thus, $K_p = K_c(RT)^{0} = K_c$.

For (D): Solids are not included. $\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 0 = 2$. Thus, $K_p = K_c(RT)^{2}$.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the reaction $\mathrm{CaCO}_3(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CaO}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g})$ at $1000 \mathrm{~K}$, the numerical value of $K_P$ is less than $K_C$.

Reason (R): For the given reaction, the change in the number of moles of gaseous species ($\Delta n_g$) is positive and at $1000 \mathrm{~K}$, the value of $RT$ is greater than $1$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
The relationship between $K_P$ and $K_C$ is given by $K_P = K_C(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$.

For the reaction $\mathrm{CaCO}_3(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CaO}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g})$, the change in gaseous moles is:
$\Delta n_g = n_{g(\text{products})} - n_{g(\text{reactants})} = 1 - 0 = 1$.

Since $\Delta n_g = 1$, we have $K_P = K_C(RT)^1$.

At $1000 \mathrm{~K}$, the value of $R$ is approximately $0.0831 \mathrm{~L~bar~K^{-1}~mol^{-1}}$, so $RT = 0.0831 \times 1000 = 83.1$, which is greater than $1$.

Because $RT \gt 1$ and $\Delta n_g = 1$, it follows that $K_P = K_C \times 83.1$, meaning $K_P \gt K_C$.

Thus, Assertion (A) is incorrect because it states $K_P \lt K_C$. Reason (R) is correct as $\Delta n_g$ is positive and $RT \gt 1$.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given the equilibrium constants for the following base reactions:
$X \rightleftharpoons Y ; K$
$Z \rightleftharpoons W ; K'$

Match the reactions in List-I with their corresponding equilibrium constants in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) $Y \rightleftharpoons X$(I) $K^2$
(B) $2X \rightleftharpoons 2Y$(II) $\dfrac{1}{K}$
(C) $\dfrac{1}{2} Y \rightleftharpoons \dfrac{1}{2} X$(III) $K \times K'$
(D) $X + Z \rightleftharpoons Y + W$(IV) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{K}}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For a base reaction $X \rightleftharpoons Y$ with equilibrium constant $K$:

(A) When the reaction is reversed ($Y \rightleftharpoons X$), the new equilibrium constant is the reciprocal of the original. Thus, $K_{new} = \dfrac{1}{K}$. Matches with (II).

(B) When the reaction is multiplied by 2 ($2X \rightleftharpoons 2Y$), the new equilibrium constant is the original raised to the power of 2. Thus, $K_{new} = K^2$. Matches with (I).

(C) When the reaction is reversed and multiplied by $\dfrac{1}{2}$ ($\dfrac{1}{2} Y \rightleftharpoons \dfrac{1}{2} X$), the new equilibrium constant is the reciprocal raised to the power of $\dfrac{1}{2}$. Thus, $K_{new} = \left(\dfrac{1}{K}\right)^{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{K}}$. Matches with (IV).

(D) When two reactions are added ($X + Z \rightleftharpoons Y + W$), their equilibrium constants are multiplied. Thus, $K_{new} = K \times K'$. Matches with (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II for the expression of $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ in terms of forward rate constant ($\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}$), backward rate constant ($\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}$), $\mathrm{R}$, and $\mathrm{T}$.

List I (Reaction)List II ($\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ expression)
(A) $\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{HI}(\mathrm{g})$(I) $\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}\right)(\mathrm{RT})^{-2}$
(B) $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g})$(II) $\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}\right)$
(C) $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$(III) $\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}\right)(\mathrm{RT})^{-1}$
(D) $2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g})$(IV) $\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}\right)(\mathrm{RT})^{1}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For any reaction, the equilibrium constant in terms of concentration is $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}$.

The relationship between $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is given by $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}} = \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}\right)(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}}$.

(A) $\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{HI}(\mathrm{g})$: $\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = 2 - (1+1) = 0$. Thus, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}\right)$. (Matches II)

(B) $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g})$: $\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = 2 - 1 = 1$. Thus, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}\right)(\mathrm{RT})^{1}$. (Matches IV)

(C) $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$: $\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = 2 - (1+3) = -2$. Thus, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}\right)(\mathrm{RT})^{-2}$. (Matches I)

(D) $2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g})$: $\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = 2 - (2+1) = -1$. Thus, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}}\right)(\mathrm{RT})^{-1}$. (Matches III)

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Reaction)List-II (Relation between $K_P$ and $K_C$)
(A) $\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{HI}(\mathrm{g})$(I) $K_P = K_C(RT)^{-2}$
(B) $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$(II) $K_P = K_C$
(C) $\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{HS}(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{g})$(III) $K_P = K_C(RT)^2$
(D) $\mathrm{PCl}_5(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g})$(IV) $K_P = K_C(RT)$
(V) $K_P = K_C(RT)^{-1}$

questions.solution:
The relationship between $K_P$ and $K_C$ is $K_P = K_C(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$, where $\Delta n_g = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$.

(A) $\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{HI}(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$. Therefore, $K_P = K_C$. (Matches II)

(B) $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$. Therefore, $K_P = K_C(RT)^{-2}$. (Matches I)

(C) $\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{HS}(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{g})$
Solid species are ignored in $\Delta n_g$ calculation. $\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 0 = 2$. Therefore, $K_P = K_C(RT)^2$. (Matches III)

$\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 1 = 1$. Therefore, $K_P = K_C(RT)$. (Matches IV)

The correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following equilibrium reactions at a certain temperature:
(i) $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) ; K_1$
(ii) $\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}) ; K_2$

The equilibrium constant $K_3$ for the reaction
$2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})$
in terms of $K_1$ and $K_2$ is:
questions.solution:
The target reaction is:
$2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})$

To obtain this target reaction, we manipulate the given reactions as follows:

Reverse reaction (i). The equilibrium constant becomes the reciprocal of $K_1$.
$2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) ; K' = \dfrac{1}{K_1}$

Reverse reaction (ii) and multiply it by 2. The equilibrium constant becomes the reciprocal of $K_2$, raised to the power of 2.
$2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) ; K'' = \left(\dfrac{1}{K_2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{K_2^2}$

Add the two modified reactions.
$\left[2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})\right] + \left[2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})\right]$
This yields the target reaction:
$2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})$

When reactions are added, their equilibrium constants are multiplied. Therefore, the equilibrium constant $K_3$ for the target reaction is:
$K_3 = K' \times K'' = \dfrac{1}{K_1} \times \dfrac{1}{K_2^2} = \dfrac{1}{K_1 K_2^2}$

Answer: $K_3 = \dfrac{1}{K_1 K_2^2}$

The value of $K_c$ is $2.5$ at $1000 \mathrm{~K}$. What will be the value of $K_p$ for this reaction at the same temperature?
(Given: $\mathrm{R} = 0.083 \mathrm{~L~bar~K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
For the given heterogeneous reaction:
$3\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s}) + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Fe}_3\mathrm{O}_4(\mathrm{s}) + 4\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g})$

The change in the number of moles of gaseous species ($\Delta n_g$) is calculated by considering only the gaseous products and reactants, strictly ignoring the solid species.
$\Delta n_g = \text{moles of } \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) - \text{moles of } \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta n_g = 4 - 4 = 0$

The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by:
$K_p = K_c(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta n_g}$

Substituting $\Delta n_g = 0$:
$K_p = K_c(\mathrm{RT})^0 = K_c$

Therefore, $K_p = 2.5$.

Including solid species in the calculation would incorrectly give $\Delta n_g = -2$, leading to the wrong answer $3.6 \times 10^{-4}$.

Answer: $2.5$

$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AgCl} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Ag}^{+}+\mathrm{Cl}^{-} \\ & K_2^{\prime}=\frac{1}{K_2}=\frac{1}{5.4 \times 10^9}\end{aligned}$
Now for the reaction,
$\mathrm{AgCl}+2 \mathrm{NH}_3 \rightleftharpoons\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{+}+\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\begin{aligned} K=K_1 \times K_2^{\prime} & =1.7 \times 10^7 \times \frac{1}{5.4 \times 10^9} \\ & =0.31 \times 10^{-2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The dissociation equilibrium of a gas $A B_2$ can be represented as
$2 A B_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 A B(g)+B_2(g)$
The degree of dissociation is ' $x$ ' and is small compared to 1 . The expression relating the degree of dissociation ( $x$ ) with equilibrium constant $K_p$ and total pressure $p$ is
questions.solution:
\(\begin{array}{cccc} 
& 2 A B_2(g) & \rightleftharpoons & 2 A B(g) & + & B_2(g) \\
\text {Initial moles } & 1 & & 0 & & 0 \\
\text {At equilibrium } & 2(1-x) & & 2 x & & x
\end{array}\)
where, $\quad x=$ degree of dissociation
$\begin{aligned}\text { Total moles at equilibrium } & =2-2 x+2 x+x \\& =(2+x)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { So, } \quad \rho_{A B_2}= \frac{2(1-x) p}{(2+x)} \\ & \rho_{A B}=\frac{2 x p}{(2+x)}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} p_{B_2} & =\frac{x p}{(2+x)} \\ K_p & =\frac{\left(p_{A B}\right)^2\left(p_{B_2}\right)}{\left(p_{A B_2}\right)^2}\end{aligned}=\frac{\left(\frac{2 x p}{2+x}\right)^2\left(\frac{x}{2+x} p\right)}{\left(\frac{2(1-x)}{(2+x)} p\right)^2}=\frac{x^3 p}{(2+x)(1-x)^2}\begin{aligned} {[\because x \ll 1 \text { and } 2 \text {, so }} & (1-x)=1,(2+x)=2] \\ & =\frac{x^3 p}{2}\end{aligned}x=\left(\frac{2 K_p}{p}\right)^{1 / 3}$

questions.q:
The value of $K_c$ for the reaction,
$2 A \rightleftharpoons B+C$ is $2 \times 10^{-3}$. At a given time, if the composition of reaction mixture is $[A]=[B]=[C]=3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$. Which is true?
options: The reaction will proceed in forward direction
The reaction will proceed in backward direction
The reaction will proceed in any direction
questions.solution:
Reaction quotient, $Q_C=[B][C] /[A]^2$ as
as
$[A]=[B]=[C]=3 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{M}Q_C=\left(3 \times 10^{-4}\right) \times\left(3 \times 10^{-4}\right) /\left(3 \times 10^{-4}\right)^2=1$
As $Q_C \gt K_c$, so the reaction will proceed in the reverse direction.

questions.q: In III group precipitation, $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ is added before adding $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ to
questions.solution:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Equilibrium constants $K_1$ and $K_2$ for the following equilibria $\mathrm{NO}(g)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 \stackrel{K_1}{\rightleftharpoons} \mathrm{NO}_2(g)$ and $2 \mathrm{NO}_2(g) \stackrel{K_2}{\rightleftharpoons} 2 \mathrm{NO}(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g)$ are related as
questions.solution:
(i) $\mathrm{NO}(g)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(g) \stackrel{K_1}{\rightleftharpoons} \mathrm{NO}_2(g)$
So $K_1=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]}{[\mathrm{NO}]\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}}...(i)$
(ii) $2 \mathrm{NO}_2(g) \stackrel{K_2}{\rightleftharpoons} 2 \mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{O}_2(g)$
So $K_2=\frac{[\mathrm{NO}]^2\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]}{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2}...(ii)$
From Eq. (i)
$K_1^2=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2}{\left[\mathrm{NO]}^2\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]\right.}$
or $\frac{1}{K_1^2}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}\right]^2\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]}{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2}...(iii)$
From Eqs. (ii) and (iii)
$K_2=\frac{1}{K_1^2}$

questions.solution: $K_c=\frac{[C][D]}{[A][B]}=\frac{2 x \times 2 x}{x \times x}=4$
